note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (500 rows, t1_right/t2_right stored as ints 0/1, read as true iff == 1; cap flags are bools) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (committed, no fetch). k4 = attempt-0 rows, first in file order per (problem_index, sample) for samples 0-3, right = score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit (cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing/null and finish_reason 'length'); a missing row counts as not right. Strata 0, 1, 2, {3,4}; C problems whose stratum has no F problem are dropped; expected = mean of r_F over the remaining C problems (so it is weighted by C's stratum mix). n = all kept problems (C + F), because r_F uses the F problems too. The bootstrap resamples kept problems and recomputes r_F, the dropping and the difference; a resample with no C problem left scores 0.0 (very unlikely with this many cap hits). Alternative reading (alt_measured): a cap-hit answer whose score is right counts as right everywhere (T1-right, RL right and the k4 count), so C holds only the T1 cap hits that are wrong by score. If no cap-hit row is scored right, alt equals the main number. Caveat: T1 (per_problem.json) and the day1_3 rows come from different base cue runs, so k4 is a separate draw from T1, not the T1 sample itself.

Files fetched from S3 (profile iterate-ecr) into runs/theory-tests/s3k/r5/<run>/<job>/answers.jsonl: e72c (B, base cue), 86ef (RL plain), and the cue arms 095e, c6c0, 3c04. The e72c and 86ef rows have no attempt field, so the first row in file order is kept (each file has one row per problem anyway). The selfdistill rows have attempt 0 only. Right = score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit not true; a null or missing score_v3 is not right. Only problems in both e72c and 86ef are kept, and then only those where B is not right. C = B cap_hit true. This puts a few B cap hits scored 1 into C, because under the recipe a cap hit is never right. F = the other not-right problems. k3 strata 0, 1, {2,3}; a missing cue row counts as not right. Same drop and expected-rate rule as k=1. n = kept problems (C + F). The bootstrap is over kept problems; a resample with no C left scores 0.0. Alternative reading (alt_measured): a cap-hit row scored 1 counts as right in every file (B, RL, the k3 arms), so those B rows leave the sample and C holds only cap hits that are wrong by score.

Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json and studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json. Both are committed, 500 rows each, and the first row per problem_index is used. Joined on problem_index, keeping rows with t1_right non-null and the sft1_cue score_v3 non-null. B right = t1_right == 1 and t1_cap_hit not true. Other right = score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit not true. Gap = other right and B not right. Statistic = gap problems with t1_cap_hit true / gap problems. n = the number of gap problems. The bootstrap resamples all joined problems and recomputes the gap and the fraction (it is a ratio with a random denominator, so it is not a binomial); an empty gap in a resample scores 0.0. Alternative reading (alt_measured): cap hits with a right score count as right on both sides, so a T1 cap hit with t1_right 1 is B-right and leaves the gap. Under the main reading such problems are in the gap and count as cap hits, which can raise the main number above the alt.
